headline: RARE EARTH STOCKS SURGE 30% IN A WEEK — USAR AND TMC REBOUND ON CRITICAL MINERALS HYPE; USAR EARNINGS AUG 10 IS NEXT CATALYST
snippet: USA Rare Earth Inc. (NASDAQ: USAR) and The Metals Company (NASDAQ: TMC) both surged approximately 30% in the week ending August 8, 2026, with Friday August 7 alone delivering gains of roughly 11% in each stock as traders re-entered the critical minerals theme ahead of near-term corporate catalysts. USAR's weekly move coincides with the completion of its two-step merger with Texas Mineral Resources, creating a combined entity focused on the Round Top heavy rare earth deposit in Texas — one of the few domestic deposits capable of producing the full suite of 47 critical minerals, including neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium, terbium, and uranium as a byproduct. USAR's Q2 2026 earnings call is scheduled for August 10, widely expected to be the first to include consolidated financials post-merger; any production update or offtake announcement would likely sustain or accelerate the recent momentum. TMC's corporate update call on August 13 is the equivalent catalyst for the seabed extraction story. The broader context: the rare earth sector spent most of H1 2026 underperforming despite China's ongoing critical mineral export restrictions — those restrictions have now tightened further, and the combination of US domestic processing ambitions, AI-driven magnet demand for EV motors and wind turbines, and a US policy environment increasingly hostile to Chinese rare earth dependence is reigniting the investment thesis that has historically produced some of the most volatile moves in the small-cap mining sector. The key risk, as ever with rare earths, is that investment thesis quality and production reality are separated by years of capital intensity — but for the speculative allocation in a retail investor's junior mining portfolio, the USAR + TMC dual-catalyst setup heading into the next two weeks is among the most time-sensitive near-term setups in the critical minerals sector.

headline: GOLDSEEK: PM SECTOR MAJOR NEW UPTREND CONFIRMED — LARGEST CYCLICAL ADVANCE IN HISTORY NOW ACCELERATING; WHAT COMES NEXT
snippet: GoldSeek's August 8 technical analysis issues a major new uptrend alert for the precious metals sector — gold, silver, and mining stocks — arguing that the week ending August 8, 2026 constitutes the technical confirmation that the sector's interrupted cyclical advance has resumed and is now in its next major leg higher. The analytical basis is rooted in gold's five-day performance from August 1–8: the metal rallied approximately 8% on the back of the -23,000 July NFP print, regaining and holding all key technical levels while GDX and GDXJ simultaneously delivered 21–22% five-day moves on heavy institutional inflows. SIL, the silver miners ETF, added 6.56% and broke decisively above the key $38–$43 resistance zone that had capped the silver mining sector for the previous four months — a resistance zone whose breach historically precedes a sustained re-rating of silver producer valuations. The analysis contextualises the current move within the broadest secular precious metals bull market since the 1970s, noting that the same structural forces that drove gold from $2,000 to $5,598 at its January 2026 all-time high — dollar debasement expectations, de-dollarisation flows, central bank accumulation, and geopolitical safe-haven demand — remain fully intact and have been reinforced by the labour market data that is now signalling a US economy weakening into an election cycle. For junior mining investors who have waited through the multi-month correction from $5,598 to $3,800 without capitulating, the GoldSeek analysis frames the current setup as the re-entry window that longer-duration cycles offer once — a view supported by the technical structure across gold, silver, SIL, GDX, and GDXJ simultaneously confirming upside breaks.

headline: EQUINOX GOLD + ORLA MINING MERGER CLOSED — EQX RAISES 2026 GUIDANCE TO 870K–920K OZ; DIVIDEND UP 50%, CEO JASON SIMPSON INCOMING
snippet: Equinox Gold Corp. (TSX/NYSE: EQX) reported August 5, 2026 strong Q2 2026 results and a fully updated operational outlook following the July 31 completion of its business combination with Orla Mining Ltd. — North America's most significant gold mining merger of 2026. Q2 standalone Equinox production was 176,836 ounces, bringing year-to-date pre-merger output to 374,464 ounces and tracking squarely within prior guidance of 700,000–800,000 ounces. Updated 2026 guidance for the combined company — capturing five months (August through December) of Orla's contribution — is 870,000 to 920,000 ounces, rising to approximately 1.1 million ounces on a full-year pro forma basis, which would place EQX firmly in the category of North America's senior gold producers alongside Kinross and Pan American. The board approved a 50% increase in the quarterly dividend to $0.09 per share annualised — one of the largest percentage dividend increases from a producer of EQX's size in 2026 — reflecting both the cash flow generation of the combined operation at $4,300+ gold and management's confidence in the forward production profile. On leadership, Darren Hall retires October 31 and Jason Simpson — former President and CEO of Orla Mining — assumes the CEO role, bringing the operational culture from Camino Rojo (Orla's flagship Mexican gold mine, one of the lowest-cost producing assets in North America) into an enlarged senior producer context. Orla shareholders approved the deal with 99.91% of votes cast. For retail investors, the merger establishes a new benchmark for what can be built through disciplined M&A in a gold bull market: a company that went from sub-400,000 oz production to a 1.1M oz annualised run-rate through a single transformative transaction at a moment when every ounce produced in North America commands a premium margin.

headline: ALBEMARLE Q2 2026: LITHIUM PRICES RECEIVED +61%, EBITDA +155% — ALB BEATS BY 24%, RAISES GUIDANCE; GREENBUSHES CGP3 BACK ONLINE
snippet: Albemarle Corporation (NYSE: ALB), the world's largest lithium producer, reported August 6, 2026 Q2 2026 results that confirmed a decisive inflection in the lithium market after nearly two years of pricing pressure: adjusted EBITDA rose 155% to $858 million, adjusted EPS of $3.75 beat consensus of $3.03 by 24%, and revenue of $1.74 billion exceeded forecasts by 9.4%. The price realisation improvement was the standout driver: the average price Albemarle received for its lithium rose 61% in Q2 year-on-year, while sales volumes increased 11% as global lithium consumption grew approximately 45% year-over-year through May 2026 — more than double the upper end of Albemarle's own forecast range of 15–40% growth. The operational update included confirmation that Greenbushes CGP3 (Albemarle's share of the world's largest hard-rock lithium mine in Western Australia, which experienced a fire June 9) restarted operations August 1 and is expected to ramp to full production by Q1 2027 — removing a supply disruption risk that had added uncertainty to H2 2026 guidance. Full-year 2026 volume guidance of 225,000–235,000 tonnes LCE was maintained. ALB shares rose 11.5% to $125.37 on the results. For junior lithium investors watching whether the commodity cycle has bottomed, Albemarle's 61% year-on-year improvement in price realisation is the most direct confirmation that the industry-wide lithium pricing floor is behind us: when the world's largest producer is selling lithium at prices 61% higher than a year ago on 45% higher consumption, the structural supply-demand dynamics that drove the 2022–2023 bull market are reasserting themselves — and junior developers in the Athabasca Basin brine plays and Australian hard rock deposits are the leveraged way to participate in the next phase of that cycle.

headline: TOCVAN VENTURES: 215M AT 0.6 g/t AU ON MEZQUITE TREND — NEAR-SURFACE DISCOVERY 1.9KM FROM PILOT FACILITY, SONORA MEXICO (TSX-V: TOC)
snippet: Tocvan Ventures Corp. (TSX-V: TOC) reported August 6, 2026 a significant new near-surface gold-silver discovery on the 1.2-kilometre El Mezquite Trend at its 100%-owned Gran Pilar Project in Sonora, Mexico. Hole JES-26-155, one of the best intercepts drilled on the project to date, returned 215 metres of 0.6 g/t gold from just 36.6 metres depth — interpretable as an upper zone of 86.9 metres at 0.6 g/t gold and a lower zone of 70.2 metres at 0.9 g/t gold, separated by a continuously anomalous interval rather than waste. High-grade intervals within the broader envelope include 1.5 metres at 16.0 g/t gold and 57 g/t silver, confirming the presence of bonanza-grade shoots within the bulk-mineable mineralised system. The strategic significance of the location is equally important: the new Mezquite discovery is 1,900 metres east of Tocvan's planned pilot production facility along existing road infrastructure — a proximity that means any resource defined here would be accessible through infrastructure already planned and partially permitted, substantially lowering the capital intensity of a future production decision. Gran Pilar's geological model has evolved to encompass multiple near-surface oxide gold-silver zones amenable to open-pit or heap-leach recovery scenarios, and the Mezquite corridor is the newest addition to that multi-zone picture. For junior investors tracking projects approaching pilot production milestones, a 215-metre bulk-mineable intercept from 36.6 metres depth — heap-leach amenable, near-surface, with bonanza-grade internal intervals, and 1.9 km from planned plant infrastructure — represents the type of discovery that directly extends the mine life and economics of a project that was already approaching its first production decision.

headline: NGEX MINERALS WRAPS LUNAHUASI PHASE 4 — 17.83% CuEq OVER 20.5M CAPS PROGRAM; PHASE 5 STEP-OUTS PLANNED FOR ONE OF ANDES' RICHEST SYSTEMS
snippet: NGEx Minerals Ltd. (TSX: NGEx) reported August 6, 2026 in its Q2 2026 results that the Phase 4 drill program at its 100%-owned Lunahuasi copper-gold-silver high-sulphidation epithermal deposit in San Juan Province, Argentina has been completed — 27,318 metres in 32 holes — and confirmed that Phase 4 expanded the high-grade Saturn, Mars, and Jupiter zones while extending the area of stockwork and disseminated porphyry mineralisation that wraps around the central high-sulphidation core. Phase 4's defining intercept, from hole results announced July 30: 20.50 metres at 17.83% copper equivalent and 13.50 metres at 11.36% copper equivalent — among the highest-grade copper-equivalent intercepts from any deposit globally in 2026. These extraordinary grades reflect the dual mineralisation style at Lunahuasi: a central high-sulphidation epithermal zone hosting ultra-high-grade gold-copper-silver (previous highlight: 17.3 metres at 207.79 g/t gold, 2.02% copper), surrounded by an expanding porphyry shell with disseminated copper-gold mineralisation that provides bulk-tonnage resource tonnage context to the bonanza core. Phase 5 planning is underway — expected to include continued step-out drilling, follow-up on newly identified zones within Phase 4, and testing of additional exploration targets identified from Phase 4 geological data — with NGEx targeting underground development commencement subject to permit timelines in Q4 2026. Located 10 kilometres south of the Los Helados copper-gold porphyry project in the Vicuña District — which the Lundin Group has assembled into one of the most significant copper-gold districts developed in South America in the past decade — Lunahuasi's compound discovery of both an ultra-high-grade epithermal core and an expanding porphyry shell positions it as potentially one of the most valuable near-term advanced exploration assets in the Andes.

headline: B2GOLD Q2: 203K OZ ABOVE GUIDANCE ON LOW AISC — MENANKOTO EXPLOITATION PERMIT EXPECTED IMMINENTLY FROM MALI (TSX/NYSE: BTG)
snippet: B2Gold Corp. (TSX/NYSE: BTG, NSX: B2G) reported August 6, 2026 Q2 2026 consolidated gold production of 203,648 ounces — above consensus expectations — with higher than expected output and lower than expected all-in sustaining costs across its three flagship operations: Fekola in Mali, Masbate in the Philippines, and Otjikoto in Namibia. The most consequential disclosure in the Q2 report is forward-looking: B2Gold stated that the Menankoto exploitation permit — the critical regulatory authorisation required to develop the satellite Menankoto deposit that would extend Fekola's mine life and transform it from a resource-declining asset into a longer-duration producing mine — is expected to be issued in the near term by the Government of Mali. Menankoto's exploitation permit has been pending for an extended period as B2Gold has navigated the transition in Mali's political environment, and its imminent issuance represents a potential near-term re-rating catalyst for BTG shares specifically because Fekola's mine life extension was already modelled by analysts as a value driver — the permit is the missing piece that converts that modelled value into an executable development pathway. At $4,300+ gold, B2Gold's Q2 cash generation was among the company's strongest quarterly performances on record, and combined with Menankoto's approaching permit, the fundamental picture for BTG has materially improved relative to the market's perception during the six-month gold correction. For investors looking for dividend-paying mid-tier gold producers with a defined near-term catalyst, BTG's combination of operational delivery and Menankoto permit progression is worth monitoring closely.

headline: ALAMOS GOLD Q2: RECORD ISLAND GOLD PRODUCTION, $270M NET INCOME — ISLAND GOLD PHASE 3 EXPANSION ON SCHEDULE FOR 2025 EXIT RATE (AGI)
source_name: Yahoo Finance / Alamos Gold Earnings Call
snippet: Alamos Gold Inc. (TSX/NYSE: AGI) reported Q2 2026 consolidated gold production of 130,600 ounces — 5% above Q1 2026 and in line with the company's revised quarterly guidance — with standout performance at the Island Gold Mine in Ontario, where record quarterly production was achieved as the Phase 3 expansion ramp continues on schedule. Net earnings for Q2 2026 reached $270 million ($0.64 per share), one of Alamos Gold's strongest quarterly results on record, generated at AISC levels significantly below the current $4,300+ gold price realisations. The Island Gold Phase 3 expansion, which will roughly triple the mine's processing throughput from 1,100 tonnes per day to over 2,000 tonnes per day, is targeting its designed exit-rate production in a near-term quarter — a transition that will make Island Gold one of Canada's highest-margin underground gold mines on a per-ounce basis. Island Gold consistently ranks among the highest-grade and lowest-cost operations globally, and at Phase 3 production rates against current gold prices, it will generate free cash flow levels that support Alamos Gold's broader capital allocation flexibility. For junior mining investors watching how majors and mid-tiers deploy capital at $4,300 gold, Alamos Gold represents the established-and-growing benchmark: a company that has consistently delivered on its expansion timeline while generating record financial results — the model that junior developers with construction-ready projects aspire to replicate.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER SET UP FOR HUGE MOVE — SIL ETF SMASHES $43 RESISTANCE; SILVER TARGETING TRIPLE DIGITS BY YEAR-END, ANALYSTS SAY
snippet: A GoldSeek analysis published August 7–8, 2026 argues that the technical and fundamental setup for gold and silver has reached a confluence of signals that have historically preceded the most powerful sustained advances in the precious metals cycle — identifying the current moment as one of only a few instances in the past decade where multiple independent bullish triggers are firing simultaneously. The technical case centres on the SIL ETF (Global X Silver Miners) surging 6.56% on August 7 and breaking decisively above the $38–$43 resistance zone that had capped silver mining stocks for four months — a resistance break that, when combined with GDX and GDXJ simultaneously delivering 20%+ weekly moves, constitutes a broad sector breakout rather than isolated commodity-price momentum. On the fundamental side, the analysis highlights that the structural supply deficit in silver has now run for six consecutive years, with annual consumption consistently exceeding mine production — a deficit that is widening as solar panel demand, EV wiring, and industrial applications absorb an increasing percentage of available supply, while primary silver mine supply is constrained by silver's byproduct-mining status (most silver is a byproduct of copper, zinc, and lead mining, meaning supply does not respond quickly to silver prices). At $64.10 per ounce post-NFP, silver is still more than 80% below its 1980 inflation-adjusted all-time high, and at least one analyst cited in the piece projects silver returning to triple-digit prices before year-end 2026 — a target that would imply a gold-silver ratio compression from the current ~67x toward the 30–40x range historically seen at precious metals cycle peaks.

headline: ALLIED GOLD Q2: KURMUK GOLD MINE IN ETHIOPIA NEARING START-UP — FINANCIAL POSITION STRENGTHENED; H1 PRODUCTION 193K OZ (TSXV: AGLD)
snippet: Allied Gold Corp. (TSX: AGLD) reported August 5, 2026 Q2 2026 results showing adjusted earnings of $55.4 million ($0.44 per basic share), with first-half 2026 production of 193,445 gold ounces across its operating portfolio in Côte d'Ivoire and Ethiopia. The headline catalyst disclosed in the report is operational rather than financial: the Kurmuk Gold Mine in Ethiopia's Benishangul-Gumuz Region is nearing commercial production start-up — a milestone that will expand Allied Gold's producing asset base from a single-country to a diversified two-country African gold producer. Kurmuk is an advanced heap-leach open-pit gold operation targeting initial production of approximately 200,000 ounces per year, which would more than double Allied Gold's total production capacity when combined with the Bonikro Mine in Côte d'Ivoire. For investors tracking new mine start-ups in the current gold price environment, the timing of Kurmuk's commissioning is structurally optimal: commissioning a 200,000 oz/year heap-leach mine at $4,300+ gold — rather than at $2,000 as the project was originally financed — means the first-year cash flows against initial capex will recover invested capital materially faster than projected. The company's strengthened financial position noted in the Q2 report provides runway to manage the ramp-up without dilutive financing. Allied Gold's dual-country African growth story, with Kurmuk commissioning as the near-term catalyst and a strengthened balance sheet to manage the ramp, is a different risk profile than earlier-stage explorers — it offers institutional-quality mine construction execution risk rather than exploration risk, against a gold backdrop that makes execution risk the primary remaining variable.
